auditor_jane: Quick SOC2 ask — we need a chain-of-custody package for the vuln triage (INC-2025-03). Specifically: RBAC change diff + approval evidence, KMS wrap/unwrap audit logs for the affected service account key, SIEM export showing access timeline, and a signed manifest. Can you point to artifacts or assemble a pack?

maria (eng-security): On it. I'll gather items and produce a signed artifact. Quick notes: the RBAC change was PR #482 in infra repo, approvers were @devon and @samir. I can export the k8s audit, CloudTrail/KMS logs, and the Splunk/SIEM slice. cc @devon @samir

maria (eng-security): PR link: https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra/commit/6f4a2b3 (this contains the rolebinding delta and the codeowner approval history)

devon (sre): For the SIEM slice I usually run this Splunk query around the incident window:
```
index=cloudtrail eventName IN (Decrypt,GenerateDataKey,GenerateDataKeyWithoutPlaintext) keyId="arn:aws:kms:us-west-2:123456789012:key/cmk-1234" | sort _time
```
That will show GenerateDataKey and Decrypt ops. We'll export as CSV and push to s3://redwood-evidence/exports/INC-2025-03/

samir (infra): KMS notes — we used envelope encryption for the service account secrets. The workflow: app requests GenerateDataKey, receives plaintext data key, encrypts payload locally, then we only store encrypted data key (Encrypt). During read, Decrypt is called. So proof of access = CloudTrail events with eventName=Decrypt or GenerateDataKey. Sample CloudTrail/KMS line (redacted):
```
eventTime=2025-03-14T10:14:22Z eventName=Decrypt userIdentity.principalId=sts::AID... sourceIPAddress=54.23.12.34 resource=key/cmk-1234 requestParameters.keyId=arn:aws:kms:us-west-2:123456789012:key/cmk-1234
```

maria (eng-security): k8s audit path: s3://redwood-logs/k8s-audit/2025/03/14/audit-10-*.json.gz. The RBAC rolebinding change is in the infra PR (above) and the approval was in GitHub reviews (codeowner + security-review). I'll attach the review screenshot in the pack.

evidence-bot: Export job started -> pack id=pack-1765004321, files=[rbac-diff.txt, k8s-audit-slice.json.gz, cloudtrail-kms.csv, siem-slice.csv, manifest.txt], destination=s3://redwood-evidence/exports/pack-1765004321.tar.gz

oncall-juno: Incident timeline (brief):
- 2025-03-14T09:58Z: CVE flagged by triage tool -> INC-2025-03 opened
- 2025-03-14T10:12Z: RBAC change PR opened to remove broad SA role (PR #482)
- 2025-03-14T10:18Z: PR approved and merged (codeowner + sec signoff)
- 2025-03-14T10:14Z - 2025-03-14T10:45Z: Relevant KMS events (GenerateDataKey / Decrypt) — exported by @devon
- 2025-03-14T11:00Z: Postfix checks and sampling completed
All checks show no lateral escalation.

maria (eng-security): For the signed manifest: we will include SHA256 checksums for each file and sign the manifest with our internal GPG key (key id 0xA1B2C3D4). Example manifest line:
```
pack-1765004321/rbac-diff.txt  e3b0c44298fc1c149afbf4c8996fb924...
```
I'll upload presigned link and attach GPG signature.

auditor_jane: Thanks. Two clarifications: (1) Is the CMK single-tenant for this workload or shared across other services? (2) For sampling, is a 24h window acceptable (12h before/after merge)? Also we need a short mapping doc that ties each artifact to SOC2 control language (CC6.1 / CC7.3 etc).

samir (infra): CMK is shared within the account but key usage is tagged; the CMK policy restricts Decrypt to a set of principals (we'll include the policy snippet). We'll add a mapping note: GenerateDataKey => confidentiality control, Decrypt => key access control.

devon (sre): 24h window is fine. I'll attach the Splunk exported CSV and the query used as proof. Export path will be s3://redwood-evidence/exports/INC-2025-03/splunk-export-24h.csv

maria (eng-security): Ack. We'll produce the evidence bundle and mapping doc by EOD PST and post a presigned S3 link here. If auditor_jane wants specific hashes or a different signer, let me know.

auditor_jane: SHA256 manifest + GPG sig is perfect. Please include a short README that maps each file to the SOC2 control clause. Thanks all. :pray:
